To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The thyroid glands of representatives from all major vertebrate classes tested responded specifically to thyrotropin (TSH) from mammalian, sea-turtle, and ostrich pituitary glands, but occasionally showed a lack of specificity to bullfrog TSH.
the specificity of thyrotropic response varies distinctly between vertebrate classes, and within each class, between species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the specificity of thyroidal responses to pituitary hormones in amphibians, reptiles, and birds.
the evolution of the functional specificity of thyroid response.
the evolution of the functional specificity of pituitary hormone-receptor interaction in the vertebrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the specificity for thyrotropins is not a general rule, but rather a rule with exceptions.
the specificity of thyrotropic response is determined by the phylogenic relationship of the species tested.
the thyroid gland is specific for thyrotropic glycoprotein hormones, but not for their subunits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in amphibians and reptiles, thyrotropin is the sole thyrotropic hormone, whereas in birds, LH also exhibits thyrotropic activity.
the thyroid gland of vertebrates has evolved in a direction of increasing specificity for thyrotropins, but that this evolution has not been uniform among the classes.
the thyroid response to pitutary glycoprotein hormone is not as specific as the gonadal response to these hormones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the specificity of the TSH receptor is a very complex and dynamic system, and it is not surprising that it can be easily altered by mutations.
the thyroid gland is a sensitive and reliable indicator of phylogenetic relationships among animals.

the specificity of thyrotropin action on thyroid gland varies distinctly among representatives from different vertebrate classes, and that independent evolution of this functional characteristic has occurred to different extents within each class.
